newsitem.title: UK: UK govt to make brisk start on legislative plans.
newsitem.headline: UK govt to make brisk start on legislative plans.

text.p: The government intends to make a brisk start to its legislative programme for the last, truncated session of parliament by publishing most of its 13 proposed bills by the end of next week, ministers said on Wednesday.

They said bills would be published this week which would combat crime, widen the scope of the National Heritage Memorial Fund, let local authorities cut business rates on rural shops, tighten merchant shipping standards and reform ownership of Scottish crofts.

Although the government has not included plans to curb stalking and crack down on paedophiles in its programme, ministers said they would support legislation in both areas via the route of private member's bills.
Only eight days have been set aside in the parliamentary session for private member's bills, including four for second readings, when the principle of legislation is debated.
But ministers said there was no reason why private member's bills with strong cross-party support could not be passed before the general election, which must be held by May 22.
One minister described the legislative programme, announced earlier by Queen Elizabeth in a formal speech to both houses of parliament, as positive, substantial and forward-looking.
"If ever a Queen's Speech revealed a government in its tormented, twilight days, it is this," Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said.
He said the proposed laws were driven more by what would wrong-foot the opposition parties than what was right for the country.
"What people are crying out for is a message of hope and a strategy for Britian's long-term future. All they got today is a tactical plan for short-term Tory survival," Ashdown said in a statement.
